package_info.package_manager: custom Java application (no public package manager)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (example code, but applies to any version where this pattern is present)
package_info.why_malicious: The package contains a class that overrides the readObject() method to execute arbitrary code during deserialization, enabling attackers to trigger code execution by supplying crafted serialized objects. This violates the expected safe behavior of deserialization and can be exploited for remote code execution.

required_permissions: runtime execution (to execute code via command.run())

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During deserialization, the overridden readObject() method is automatically invoked, which first restores object fields using in.defaultReadObject(), then immediately calls command.run() on a deserialized field, resulting in execution of attacker-controlled code.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The readObject() method is a Java deserialization hook that is called automatically when an object is deserialized. In this code, it executes command.run() on a field that can be attacker-controlled, enabling arbitrary code execution as soon as a crafted object is deserialized.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Standard deserialization should only restore object state and not execute arbitrary code. Overriding readObject() to invoke methods on deserialized fields, especially without validation, is a clear violation of safe deserialization practices.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: readObject() is legitimately overridden to perform custom deserialization logic, such as input validation or data transformation, but not to execute untrusted or attacker-supplied code.
key_indicators: Overridden readObject() method in a Serializable class
Invocation of methods (e.g., command.run()) on deserialized fields within readObject()
No validation or restriction on the command field before execution

execution_context.trigger: During deserialization (as part of gadget chain)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During deserialization, when the run() method is invoked as part of the gadget chain, the code executes an operating system command specified by the command field using Runtime.getRuntime().exec(), resulting in arbitrary command execution on the host.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The run() method executes a command string directly via Runtime.getRuntime().exec() without any validation or restriction, and is triggered automatically through the deserialization gadget chain, allowing attackers to execute arbitrary system commands.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal deserialization and use of Runnable should not result in execution of arbitrary system commands, especially from untrusted serialized data. This implementation allows attacker-supplied input to be executed as code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate Command pattern classes may use run() to execute predefined, safe actions, but should never execute unvalidated, attacker-controlled commands.
key_indicators: Use of Runtime.getRuntime().exec() with unvalidated input in run()
Class implements both Runnable and Serializable for use in gadget chains
No input validation or restriction on the command field

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts a serialized Gadget object with a Command object as the command field, specifying a malicious command string.
Application deserializes the crafted object, triggering the readObject() method in Gadget.
The run() method of the Command object is executed, which calls Runtime.getRuntime().exec() with the attacker-supplied command.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary code execution on the target system

behavioral_signatures: Overridden readObject() methods in Serializable classes that invoke methods on deserialized fields
Deserialization of objects containing fields of type Runnable or similar interfaces that can trigger code execution
Use of Runtime.getRuntime().exec() or similar APIs within deserialization code paths
file_indicators: Java classes (e.g., Gadget.java) with readObject() methods that execute code on deserialized fields
Serialized files (e.g., .ser) containing manipulated or attacker-controlled fields, especially those referencing Runnable or Command objects
network_indicators: Unusual outbound connections or command-and-control traffic initiated by Java processes following deserialization events (if attacker command includes network activity)
Unexpected network activity from Java applications immediately after deserialization
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Use static analysis to identify Java classes that override readObject() and invoke methods on deserialized fields, particularly those leading to code execution (e.g., Runnable.run(), ProcessBuilder, or Runtime.exec()). Scan serialized object files for unexpected or manipulated data, such as fields referencing attacker-supplied classes. Monitor runtime behavior for execution of system commands during or immediately after deserialization. Employ allow-lists for deserializable classes and enforce serialization filters to block dangerous types. Correlate deserialization events with subsequent process or network activity to detect exploitation attempts.
